original_test_intent: Verify the exact SUT serial-port connector and approved cable mechanically mate and unmate within the assembly specification without pin damage, binding, looseness, retention failure or interference with surrounding chassis/riser/cable structures.
original_method: In a safe powered/ESD-controlled state, a trained operator identifies the correct connector/cable/assembly drawing, photographs precondition, inspects pin/housing/keep-out areas, performs the approved finite gentle insertion/removal check, restores final routing and documents fit/force/clearance/defects.
manual_activity: A trained operator physically inspects and mates/unmates the specified serial connector using the approved cable and assembly/ESD controls; the owner reviews any fit/force/interference defect.
required_inputs: Exact SUT/board/serial connector location, manufacturer/part and assembly drawing revision
Approved mating cable/plug, orientation/keying, retention/latch/screw method and pinout/electrical level
Safe power/ESD/handling procedure and access/cover/riser assembly state
Acceptable insertion/removal force or qualitative fit standard and finite cycle count
safety_requirements: Use safe power/ESD state and verify exact keyed orientation before contact
Inspect pins/housing first and stop on damage, misalignment, binding or excessive force
Never force, twist or repeatedly cycle an ambiguous connector
Preserve baseline/photos/logs instead of clearing unrelated evidence
Restore approved final routing/retention and isolate/rework any defect
agent_execution_scope: Assist with checklist, photo labeling, artifact hashing and defect-record completeness
Compare operator observations to supplied force/clearance/routing criteria
Keep this variant separate from BF4 mechanical, console functional and communication evidence
Perform no physical connection/manipulation or remote substitution
Make no DUT verdict without operator/owner evidence
engineer_actions: Provide connector/cable/assembly/force/clearance criteria and safe handling plan
Supervise or accept physical inspection and disposition any damage/interference
Review photos/observations and issue PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: No command can perform this physical inspection. DeepSeek's manual boundary is correct, but its Mellanox BF4 component and photos belong to row 2193, not this serial-port variant.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use the owner-approved physical inspection checklist and finite plug/unplug procedure; automation only organizes photos and observations.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Serial-port cable installation, tight/loose fit, chassis/cable/riser interference, plug/unplug criterion and 5/5-minute estimates remain.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Bind labeled before/during/after photos to connector/cable part identities and an inspection matrix for pins, keying, retention, force, strain relief, cover/riser clearance and restored routing.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds exact assembly identity, safe-state/ESD, finite cycle and defect/rework controls while removing copied BF4 scope and log clearing.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A successful electrical/console session cannot prove acceptable mechanical force/clearance, and BF4 photos cannot prove the serial connector; direct variant-specific physical evidence is essential.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Qualitative too tight/loose criteria are operator-dependent unless the assembly standard provides a force range. No remote observation can fully replace tactile/clearance inspection.

project_override_considerations: If no numeric force specification exists, the owner must approve a controlled qualitative rubric and trained-operator judgment rather than inventing a threshold.
expected_evidence: Exact source row/variant/hash and explicit separation from row 2193 BF4 variant
Before photos of pins/housing/clearance and during/final mating/routing photos
Recorded insertion/removal fit, retention, interference, strain relief and finite cycle observations
Defect/rework disposition, restored final assembly and operator/owner verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Master targets the SUT Serial Port, while source AI commands/logs explicitly target Mellanox BF4 Board—the other same-code row 2193. The copied scope is rejected and cannot contribute evidence to this variant.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Physical access and assembly criteria are execution prerequisites; the static review is complete and variant identity is reliable.

review_improvement: Corrects same-code cross-row contamination and makes the serial connector's tactile/clearance acceptance evidence exact, safe and auditable.
independent_technical_reasoning: Mechanical fit is component- and mating-pair-specific: BF4 board observations cannot transfer to a serial connector even when a code is duplicated. The source asks for tight/loose and interference judgment, which requires touch and line-of-sight across final cover/riser/routing states. A finite gentle cycle avoids creating wear while still observing insertion/removal behavior. Since no numeric force is supplied, the result must remain operator/owner-owned under an approved rubric rather than being guessed by automation.
